provenance.notes: Clean family batch, rfq archetype override. Northern-state seasonal contracts signed late summer, so the buyer is a property or facilities manager and the products lean on service logs and storm-day dispatch. No equipment or material brands, no liability advice. Fresh Fern fails CTA contrast. Ranges are planning figures, not quotes.

pageStructurePlus.section: Per push, per event or seasonal snow contracts
pageStructurePlus.contains: How each contract type is billed, trigger depths like a two-inch trigger, seasonal caps and overages, and which properties each type suits
pageStructurePlus.why: Property managers compare snow bids by contract type before price. Explaining the options up front makes the bid easy to line up against others.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Pre-treatment before storms, salt and liquid brine options, sidewalk and entrance crews, refreeze checks, and how de-icing material use is logged
pageStructurePlus.why: Ice, not snow, is what managers lose sleep over. A written ice plan answers the question every commercial buyer asks first.

pageStructurePlus.section: Storm-day service logs and site photos
pageStructurePlus.contains: Time-stamped arrival and departure logs per site, before-and-after photos, plowing and salting notes, and how managers receive them after every storm
pageStructurePlus.why: Managers need records after a storm for owners and insurers. Showing the log format wins contracts from crews who can't prove a visit.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Seasonal driveway plowing by subdivision, priority windows before work commutes, driveway marker stakes, walkway shovelling add-ons and the sign-up deadline
pageStructurePlus.why: Homeowners buy snow removal once a year in autumn. A clear plan page with a deadline fills the residential route before the first storm.

pageStructurePlus.section: Snow relocation, hauling and roof snow
pageStructurePlus.contains: Where snow gets piled on each lot, loader stacking, hauling snow off-site after big storms, and roof snow removal for flat commercial roofs
pageStructurePlus.why: Big lots run out of room by midwinter. Buyers with tight sites pick the contractor who explains where the snow will go.

openers.line: Your Google listing has snow removal reviews and no Website button, so a property manager pulling three snow bids for next winter has nothing to send to the owner.
openers.hook: Open their Maps listing and confirm there is no Website button. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: What a property manager would land on: {demo-link}

openers.line: The website link on your listing opens Facebook, where last winter's plowing videos sit next to summer landscaping posts. A facilities buyer can't tell you do commercial snow.
openers.hook: Tap their Website link. Note where it lands and whether snow work shows up without scrolling.
openers.linkLine: A snow page built for the commercial buyer: {demo-link}

openers.line: The site on your listing is a free page with a snow contract form that doesn't send. In September, that form is how next winter's lots get signed.
openers.hook: Open the site and find one broken thing: a dead form, an old number, last season's prices. Note it.
openers.linkLine: A snow contract request that actually sends: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your snow removal site wouldn't load the service list on my phone. Managers check vendors between site walks, phone in hand.
openers.hook: Only if they have a site. Load it on your phone and note what breaks. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: Snow and ice management, rebuilt for a phone: {demo-link}

openers.line: There's no way to request a snow plowing bid online with the lot size, trigger depth and sidewalk needs, so a manager has to chase you by phone in August.
openers.hook: Check the listing and any site for a bid or contract form. If there is none, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A snow bid request that asks the right questions: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your overnight plowing videos of clean lots at dawn are the best proof a snow contractor has, and they vanish from the feed by spring.
openers.hook: Find one plowing or salting video and note the property type. Name it if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Your snow work on a capability page that stays: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your reviews say the lot was clear before the first shift arrived. That's the sentence a facilities manager wants to read next to a snow bid.
openers.hook: Read their reviews and copy one phrase about timing or ice. Quote it back if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Your snow reviews next to the bid request: {demo-link}

openers.line: Commercial snow contracts get signed in late summer and early autumn. The snow contractors a manager can find online that month make the shortlist.
openers.hook: Use from July to early October. Name the month.

openers.line: Homeowners decide on a driveway snow plan the week of the first forecast. A sign-up page with your route areas and a deadline fills the plow route before you get the call.
openers.hook: Use from September to the first snowfall. Check whether they do residential driveways.

openers.line: Saw you're hiring plow drivers and shovelers for the season. Good applicants check whether the snow outfit looks steady before signing up for 3am call-outs.
openers.hook: Only if they posted a hiring note or a sign. Note the date.
openers.linkLine: A snow company page with a seasonal hiring section: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your snow reviews come from {Neighborhood} and a few business parks, but nothing online shows where your plow routes run, so managers outside them never ask.
openers.hook: Find the areas named in their posts or reviews and use the one furthest from their yard.
openers.linkLine: A coverage map for your snow routes: {demo-link}

openers.line: A seasonal snow contract paid in monthly instalments is easier to approve than one big invoice. If you offer that, it belongs on the contract page.
openers.hook: Only if they mention monthly billing or instalments. Never name a lender.

openers.line: Every property manager asks a snow contractor for a certificate of insurance before signing. A page that says you carry the coverage answers it early.
openers.hook: Look for 'insured' on their listing, truck or posts. Never claim coverage you didn't see.
openers.linkLine: Insurance and snow contract terms on one page: {demo-link}

openers.line: Sounds like your snow lots renew on a handshake every autumn. That works until a building changes management and the new manager searches for snow bids instead.
openers.hook: Look for posts or reviews that mention long-time clients or a manager by role. Quote it.
openers.linkLine: Where a new manager looking for snow bids should land: {demo-link}

openers.line: That {specific recent job} you posted shows how your crew handled a real storm. It belongs on a capability page a manager can forward with your snow bid.
openers.hook: Pick their newest storm post and name it: the lot, the snowfall, the hauling.
openers.linkLine: That storm on a snow capability page: {demo-link}

sequence.dm1:
Hi {Owner} — that {specific recent job} you posted is a clean storm response.

I looked for a site for {Business Name} and found the Facebook page, but nothing a property manager could forward with a snow bid. I put together a sample capability page with a contract request and a storm-day log example, with marked placeholders where your photos would go.

Would it help if I sent it over?
sequence.dm2:
{Owner} — following up in case my last message got buried. Here's the sample snow and ice site for {Business Name}: {demo-link}

It explains per-push, per-event and seasonal contracts, shows an ice management plan and a storm-day service log, and has a bid request for managers plus a driveway sign-up for homeowners. If it's not useful, tell me and I'll leave you alone.

IF NO:

IF YES:
"What did you think?"
 → let them talk, don't fill the silence
"The build runs {Build Range}, then {Care Range} a month for hosting and changes. For a snow operation your size I'd normally quote about {Build Price}, less than one commercial lot for the season."
"Can I walk you through it for ten minutes this week, before the first storm?"

CLOSE:

objections.objection: My contracts are already signed for this winter.
objections.handler: "Then build it now while it's quiet. The storm logs it shows will be your best sales tool when the next snow contract season opens."

objections.objection: All my lots come from word of mouth.
objections.handler: "That means your plowing is good. Managers still forward something to the owner before signing, and a capability page with your ice plan is easier to forward than a phone number."

objections.objection: I do landscaping in summer, I don't need a snow site.
objections.handler: "You need a snow page that doesn't look like a mowing page. Commercial buyers want trigger depths, ice plans and logs. It can live on the same domain as your summer work."

objections.objection: Snow is unpredictable, I can't publish prices.
objections.handler: "You don't publish lot prices. You explain how per-push, per-event and seasonal contracts work, and the manager sends you lot details for a bid."

objections.objection: I'm too busy once it snows.
objections.handler: "That's why this goes live before it does. I need about twenty minutes and your contract terms; after that, the site takes bid requests while you're plowing."
"{Build Range}. For you about {Build Price}, because it's the capability page, the snow bid request, the ice plan and the driveway sign-up. That's less than one commercial lot for the season."

email.subject: Snow capability page for {Business Name}

sequence.voicemail: "Hi {Owner}, it's {Your Name}. I build websites for snow and ice contractors in {City}, and I made a sample capability page for {Business Name} with a bid request and an ice plan. I'll email you the link. {Your Phone}. Thanks."
sequence.takedown:
{Owner} — I'm taking the {Business Name} snow demo down on Friday to free up the space.

Want me to leave it up? One word is fine either way.
sequence.nurture:
Hi {Owner} — the first real snow is close in {City}, and homeowners who never signed up for a driveway plan start searching the night of the forecast. Thought of you.

The site is still here whenever you want it, and nothing's changed on price. {demo-link} if you want another look.

bullets: Peg the build to less than one commercial lot for one season, never to a single driveway plan.
The capability page and bid request are the core. Price the driveway sign-up and storm-log pages around them.
Price the residential sign-up higher when it takes payment and assigns route areas; that's real workflow.
Sell before September for commercial and before the first storm for residential; nothing sells in March.
Never write liability or slip-and-fall advice into the copy; the ice plan describes service, not legal protection.
Keep monthly items low in summer, or pause them, so a seasonal business doesn't resent paying in July.

lineItems.item: Commercial snow bid request with lot details
lineItems.description: Max with lot size, sidewalk length, trigger depth, contract type, site map upload and certificate-of-insurance request.
Max with route-area check by address, plan options, walkway add-ons, payment at sign-up and a deadline banner.
Max with pre-treatment, refreeze checks, material options and a sample material use log.
Max with a realistic log layout, photo examples and how managers receive logs after each storm.
Max when each page covers a property type like medical offices, HOAs or retail, with its own snow priorities.
Max with residential route areas and commercial coverage zones, plus an address check for driveway plans.

lineItems.item: Seasonal hiring page for plow drivers
lineItems.description: Max with an applicant form, licence and equipment questions, on-call expectations and texts to the owner.

whatElseYouSell.name: Snow contract season outreach to managers
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A short campaign in July and August to property and facilities managers near your snow routes, offering a site walk and a bid."

whatElseYouSell.name: Residential snow plan sign-up campaign
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Door hangers and posts in your plow route neighbourhoods with the sign-up deadline, before the first forecast sends everyone searching."

whatElseYouSell.name: Google profile upkeep through the snow season
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Storm-morning photos of cleared lots on your Google profile all winter, and summer work posted the rest of the year, so the listing is never stale."
whatElseYouSell.when: Day 30, paused or reduced in summer.

whatElseYouSell.name: Property manager reference collection
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "After each big storm, happy managers get a short request for a review or a reference line for your next snow bid."

whatElseYouSell.name: Snow bid packet design
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A manager forwarding your snow proposal to the owner should be holding a tidy PDF: trigger terms, de-icing approach, a storm log example and your coverage certificate."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2, or before the next bid deadline they mention.

whatElseYouSell.name: Truck and plow lettering artwork
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Lettering on the plow trucks and a small sign at each commercial lot, so every manager driving past sees whose snow crew cleared it."

whatElseYouSell.name: Storm photo and drone video night
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "One storm night filming the plows and loaders at a big lot gives the snow capability page footage no competitor has."
whatElseYouSell.when: First major storm, at a property that agrees in writing.

withoutAI.route: Landscapers who sub out snow work
withoutAI.whoPays: The landscaping company, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The landscaper who passes you their winter snow accounts shows nothing online for summer work. Same capability layout."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Landscapers and snow contractors share clients across seasons and already trade referrals.

withoutAI.route: Property management firms on their routes
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Managers you plow for still email tenants a parking notice before every storm. A tenant portal for their buildings is work I can win through you."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Managers trust the vendor who shows up at four in the morning, and that trust gets a meeting.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The bulk salt yard where you load before every storm takes orders by phone. An order and pickup page is my next build."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Suppliers sell to every snow contractor in the region and have the budget for a proper site.

withoutAI.route: Roofers who need roof snow removal
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The roofer you call when a flat roof needs snow removed has an old gallery and no estimate form. Introduce me."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Roofers have big tickets and trust the snow contractor who protects their roofs.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The HOA whose streets you plow sends notices on paper. A resident site with snow-day updates and rules is a quick build."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: HOA boards trust the snow contractor residents already thank every winter.

withoutAI.whoPays: The repair shop, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The shop that fixes your plow blade mid-storm books by phone. An urgent repair request page saves them calls at 2am."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Repair shops serve every snow fleet nearby and listen when a good customer recommends you.

withAI.pitchLine: "The landscaper talks through a site walk and gets a draft maintenance estimate, the same tool built for your snow bids."
withAI.whyItWorks: Already working for a contractor the landscaper trusts, so the pitch is short.

withAI.route: Storm notice writer for property managers
withAI.pitchLine: "Before each storm, tenants get a notice about parking and plowing times, drafted from the snow contractor's schedule."
withAI.whyItWorks: Managers write the same storm notices all winter, and the snow client already knows the timing.

withAI.route: Reorder forecaster for the salt supplier
withAI.pitchLine: "Contractors see their usual salt use per storm, and the supplier gets draft reorders before the forecast hits."
withAI.whyItWorks: Suppliers run short during storms; forecasting customer orders is worth real money to them.

withAI.route: Roof load photo triage for roofers
withAI.pitchLine: "Building owners upload photos of deep roof snow, and the roofer gets a sorted list of which roofs to check first."
withAI.whyItWorks: Roofers drown in calls after big storms, and the snow client sends them those calls.

withAI.pitchLine: "Residents ask when their street gets plowed or where to park during a storm, and the assistant answers from the HOA's snow rules."
withAI.whyItWorks: Boards field these questions every storm, and the snow contractor's schedule makes the answers accurate.

withAI.route: Parts lookup for the repair shop
withAI.pitchLine: "Plow owners describe the broken part and the truck, and the shop gets a draft parts list before the truck rolls in."
withAI.whyItWorks: Storm-night repairs are rushed; anything that speeds them up sells itself.

softwareAI.name: Missed-call text-back with the snow plan link
softwareAI.pitchLine: "You're in the plow at 3am and miss a call. The caller gets a text with the driveway sign-up or the commercial snow bid form within a minute."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Day 30. Needs the business number forwarded and wording they approve. Can pause in summer.

softwareAI.name: Storm-day service log app
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Drivers tap in and out at each lot, add photos and salt amounts, and every manager gets a time-stamped snow log the morning after."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2, before the first storm. Needs the site list, crews and the log fields managers ask for.

softwareAI.name: Storm alert to residential route customers
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When a snow event triggers, driveway customers get a text that the plows are rolling and a rough window for their street."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs the route list and the trigger rules.

softwareAI.name: Snow bid calculator by lot size
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Enter the lot area, sidewalk length, trigger and contract type, and the calculator drafts the snow and ice price from your own rates."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their production rates, salt costs and margin rules.

softwareAI.name: Bid writer from site-walk notes
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Talk through the site walk in the truck, and a draft snow bid with ice plan, piling areas and price is ready when you get back."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3, during contract season. Needs past bids and the calculator's rates. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Residential route sign-up with payment
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Homeowners check their address against the plow routes, choose a plan, pay and get a driveway marker drop-off date."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2, before the sign-up deadline. Needs route areas, plans and payment setup.

softwareAI.name: Storm-night receptionist
softwareAI.pitchLine: "During a storm, 'when is my lot getting plowed' calls are answered from the live route status, so the owner stays in the truck."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3, after the service log app. Needs route status data and approved wording. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Dispatch board with live site status
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every snow site on one board, plowed, salted or waiting, with crews assigned and managers able to see their own lots."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4, once they run several crews. Needs site list, crews and the service log app.

softwareAI.name: Weather trigger watcher
softwareAI.pitchLine: "It reads the public forecast for each route area and drafts the pre-treatment and plowing plan for the owner to approve the evening before."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs route areas, trigger depths and the owner's usual storm plan. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Seasonal contract renewal reminders
softwareAI.pitchLine: "In July, every commercial snow client gets a renewal note with last winter's log summary, and every driveway customer gets the early sign-up offer."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 9, ahead of the next season. Needs contract end dates and the customer list.

softwareAI.name: Plow driver applicant screener
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Applicants for plow and shovel crews answer questions about licences, night availability and equipment, and you only call the ones who fit."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: August to October. Needs must-haves, pay and on-call rules. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Salt and material use tracker
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Salt and brine used per site per storm, so the owner bills the overages correctly and orders before the yard runs out of ice melt."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs the service log and their material costs.

softwareAI.name: Storm summary writer for managers
softwareAI.pitchLine: "After each storm, every manager gets a short plain-language summary of when their lot was plowed and salted, drafted from the log."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3, after the service log app. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Job costing per snow site
softwareAI.pitchLine: "See which lots made money this winter once truck hours, labour and salt are counted, before you rebid them."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6, at season's end. Needs a winter of logs and costs.

softwareAI.name: Driveway marker and route photo map
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every driveway on the snow route with a photo, marker positions and hazards like low walls, so a new plow driver doesn't hit anything."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2, before the first storm. Needs addresses and a drive-by photo of each driveway.

softwareAI.name: Customer message sorter for storm days
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Storm-day messages about missed driveways, plow damage and ice get sorted by urgency and drafted for the snow office to approve."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs the business inbox or text line. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Damage report intake
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A customer reports lawn or curb damage from the plow with a photo, it goes on the spring repair list, and they get a confirmation right away."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs the owner's repair policy wording.

softwareAI.name: Crew knowledge base for each snow site
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A new driver asks the phone where to pile snow at this lot or which entrance gets salted first, and gets the owner's site notes."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs written site notes and the owner's approval of every answer. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Contract proposal reader
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Drop in a manager's snow RFP, and get a summary of triggers, response times and penalties to discuss with your own advisers before bidding."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 9, during bid season. Needs a few past RFPs. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Manager portal for logs and invoices
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Property managers download every storm log, photo and snow invoice for their sites without emailing the office."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5, after the service log app. Needs client list and billing data.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Productise the storm-day service log for snow contractors
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: Snow contractors, monthly per account in season
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "I built a storm log app for one snow contractor. Every plow operator has to prove when the lot was cleared and salted."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: The first client paid for the logging workflow, and proof of service is the same problem across every northern market.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: License the snow bid calculator to a salt and ice melt distributor
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Give every snow contractor who buys salt from you a bid calculator that also estimates their material order."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Distributors compete for contractor loyalty before each season, and a tool tied to their catalog wins it.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Snow and ice contractors' association toolkit
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Offer members a capability page template with contract types, an ice plan and a sample snow log built in."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Associations want members to look professional to property managers; one agreement reaches many owners.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Everyone who buys a plow or spreader from you gets a snow business site and route sign-up to fill the new equipment."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Dealers want buyers busy enough to buy a second truck, and the snow client proves the template works.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Every snow vendor across your buildings uploads storm logs, photos and certificates to one portal you control."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Large firms chase snow records after every storm. The client's log app proves you understand it.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: White-label snow site template for agencies
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your agency builds landscaping sites that ignore winter. License my snow capability template with bid request and driveway sign-up."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Agencies already have landscaper clients who plow; the snow template is an easy add-on for them.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Retail and restaurant chains' winter vendor desk
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Every location's snow contractor, storm logs and response times on one desk, so the facilities team stops calling plow operators one by one."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Chains manage many local snow vendors and pay for a single view of them.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The town or city public works office
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Residents who can't shovel get matched to vetted local snow crews, with a request page and a log the town can check."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Towns need sidewalk help for older residents, and the snow client's logs make the program accountable.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: The same snow stack in the next northern metro
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: New snow clients in a new metro
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "I work with one snow contractor per area, and {City} has its plow crew. The next snowbelt city is open."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Non-competing geography lets you reuse the capability page, the log app and the proof.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your snow contractor clients get a service log template with the records you ask for at renewal, branded for your agency."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Agencies want well-documented clients, and the snow log is already built.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Each of your branches can sell winter snow contracts with the same capability page and driveway sign-up, built once."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Groups want year-round revenue from summer crews, and the template is ready.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "A dispatch board or storm log app nobody finished before the season? I'll get the snow workflow running before the first storm."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Stranded owners already decided to buy, and winter is a hard deadline.

upsellLadder.offer: Snow capability site plus care plan, one contract

upsellLadder.line: "The snow site and the care plan go on one contract, so a sign-up deadline banner or a storm notice is a text to me."

upsellLadder.trigger: They mention driveway customers calling to ask if there's room on the snow route.
upsellLadder.line: "Those driveway calls can sign up and pay themselves. Let's fill the plow route before the first storm."

upsellLadder.trigger: A manager asks for proof of service, or the first storm is in the forecast.
upsellLadder.line: "The first manager who asks when the lot was salted gets a time-stamped snow log instead of a guess."

upsellLadder.trigger: After the first big storm, at least one manager thanks them.
upsellLadder.line: "That manager's thank-you after the storm is a reference for next season's snow bids."

upsellLadder.offer: Dispatch board with live site status
upsellLadder.trigger: Storm-night phone calls from managers pile up, or they add a crew.
upsellLadder.line: "Those storm-night calls stop when managers can see their lot's plowing status themselves."

upsellLadder.trigger: The season ends and they start thinking about rebidding.
upsellLadder.line: "Before you rebid any lot, see which snow sites actually made money this winter."

upsellLadder.offer: Snow contract season outreach to managers
upsellLadder.trigger: July arrives, with a winter of logs and references to show.
upsellLadder.line: "Contract season is here and you have a full winter of snow logs. Let's show them to the managers who don't know you yet."
